sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned AGA for the State-respondent.

2. This application has been filed by applicant for a direction to the court concerned not to take any coercive measures arising out of Complaint Case No.686 of 2000, State Vs. Munna, under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration (PFA) Act, 1954, Police Station Dhoomanganj, District Allahabad which is pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.2,
Allahabad.

entities.text:
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.2,
Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that proceedings under Section 82 Cr.P.C. has been drawn against one Munne.
However, the applicant is not the accused against which the aforesaid proceeding has been drawn.
In this respect, an application on 4.7.2025 has been preferred before the court concerned however, till date no order has been passed.
4. Learned A.G.A. has objected to the aforesaid and submits that the applicant is Munne and the applicant is concealing its identity.

5. Be that as it may, since the dispute with regard to identity of the applicant is pending, let the court concerned decide the application dated 4.7.2025 after examining the issue within a period of one month from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.

6. Till the identity of the accused is established in respect of the applicant or the application is decided, the applicant shall not be harassed provided the applicant shall co-operate with the court concerned and appear before the court concerned.
7. The present application stands disposed of.
(Vikram D. Chauhan,J.) November 18, 2025 Bhaskar  Mohd. Masood vs State Of U.P. on 18 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29536672/
